messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert for org=bridgewater — sustained 5xxs and token latency spike. Paging @devon (oncall) — see metrics: https://grafana.internal/r/bridgewater-spike
Devon: I’m on it. Logging in now. What’s the observed error pattern? 502s or 5xx token errors?
Maria: Mostly 502 + streaming timeouts on /v1/chat/stream. Burst from a scheduled job at Bridgewater hitting thousands of short requests.
Anil: Customer reports degraded UX — their retry loop is amplifying the burst. Can we temporarily relax RL for that org while we coordinate? :grimacing:
Devon: Need quick impact estimate. Maria, can you share org QPS and error rate window?
Maria: Last 3min: peak 1.8k qps (baseline ~120 qps), 502 rate ~18%. Latency p95 for tokens jumped to 4.2s. Link: https://grafana.internal/d/bridgewater
Devon: Ok. Two mitigation options: 1) emergency org-level rate limit bump, capped duration; 2) soft-deny non-critical endpoints (attachments/preview) for bridgewater. Which minimizes customer impact? 
Anil: They rely on embeddings + chat. Attachments preview is low priority for them. If we disable previews, we reduce downstream batch pressure.
Maria: Bump buys time to stabilize batching. Recommend limited RL override: 3x for 10min, then auto-fallback to baseline with cooldown. Also throttle streaming frames per-conn to reduce concurrent decode pressure.
Devon: I’ll perform emergency override and then disable preview endpoints as a fallback. Calling the runbook: /runbooks/incident-rate-spike
Devon: @ops please stand by to monitor infra memory/GPU queues.
ops: Standing by. Watching queue_depth and kv-cache hits.
Devon: Executing hotfix now:

```
# emergency override via admin API
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/orgs/bridgewater/override-rate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{"org":"bridgewater","qps_limit":3600,"duration_seconds":600,"reason":"emergency spike - temporary bump"}'
```
deploy-bot: deploy started: override-rate v1 -> prod by devon
Devon: Override call returned 200. New soft-limit in effect. Adding streaming frame cap:

```
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/orgs/bridgewater/override-props" -d '{"stream_frame_cap":4,"duration_seconds":600}'
```
Maria: Immediately seeing drop in error rate to ~6% and p95 latency down to 1.1s. qps fell to 850 after backoff from customer side. Grafana: https://grafana.internal/r/bridgewater-after
Anil: Good. Can we also enable per-token cache warming for their common prefixes to reduce decode work? Not urgent but helpful.
Devon: Will queue a config change for cache hints; not part of hotfix.
Maria: Note: we temporarily disabled preview endpoints for bridgewater to reduce shard contention.
Devon: Command to disable previews:

```
# feature toggle
POST /admin/feature-toggle -d '{"org":"bridgewater","feature":"preview","enabled":false,"duration_seconds":900}'
```
deploy-bot: feature-toggle applied
ops: GPU queue depth stabilized, no OOMs. RX/TX latency normalizing.
Anil: Bridgewater PM notified. They confirmed retries reduced on their side and will throttle their batch job.
Devon: Putting a protective comment: emergency rate override will auto-expire in 10m. If no regression, we roll back overrides and re-enable preview. Anyone object to auto-expire flow?
Maria: fine. Create follow-up ticket to discuss longer term: customer-specific burst rules + alert thresholds.
Anil: Also recommend an opt-in burst window for partners that need scheduled high-QPS jobs.
Devon: Final steps: watch for 10m, validate error floor <1%, then rollback. If errors rise, escalate to full capacity team.
incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged by devon. Current status: mitigated (manual override + feature disable). Follow-up task: #ENG-6231 (create org-burst-policy).
